symptom: `mxcli docker --help` lists "Mendix 11.6.1 or later" as a requirement, yet `docker check` works on a Mendix 10.24 app; with an mxbuild of the project's minor but another patch, `update-widgets` fails with exit 4 and the check carries on — then ends with "Note: widget definitions were normalised on a temporary copy" a few lines after "Warning: update-widgets failed (continuing): exit status 4"
cause: The 11.6.1 floor is `docker build`'s (`build.go`, Portable App Distribution) but sat in the command group's Requirements, so it read as every subcommand's; `check` has no gate. `mx update-widgets` refuses a project whose version is not exactly mx's own ("Project is in different Mendix version - <v>", exit 4) while `mx check` accepts it, and `Check` printed its normalisation note whenever update-widgets was *requested*, not when it succeeded
insight: Exit 4 is a version mismatch, not Mendix 10: measured by relabelling a real 10.24.18 v1 project's `_MetaData._ProductVersion` to 10.24.13 — mx 10.24.18's update-widgets exits 4 with that message, its mx check reports 0 errors, and an unrelabelled project exits 0 on both (v2 and v1). `mx update-widgets --help` documents only "0 if Ok", so the message is the only diagnosis; `--loose-version-check` would upgrade the copy instead, which changes what is checked. A mismatched mx is reached easily because `ResolveMxForVersion` falls back to PATH and any cached version. A version floor in a command *group*'s help is read as every subcommand's: put it on the subcommand that enforces it, and pin the help to the enforcing line with a test. A closing note that describes a step must key on that step's outcome, not on whether it was requested
